full_judgment:
7. By responding to the Rule Nisi through an Affidavit-in-Opposition filed, the Respon- dent No. 3, Commissioner, Customs Bond Commissionerate adopts the stand that the petitioner has been evading revenue by illegally removing from its designated bonded warehouse raw materials imported under bond facility and selling the same in the local market as exposed in an investigation conducted by the office of the Respondent No. 4, Director General, Directorate of Customs Intelligence and Investigation of the petitioner’s import and export related = information/documents generated over a three-year period from 1-1- 2015 to 3]-12-207 and collected from the Customs Authority, the Bangladesh Bank's MIS and the petitioner's lien bank being Al-Arafah Islami Bank Ltd. As per the Respondent No. 3, Commissioner, an examination and verification of the available information reveals that the petitioner failed to register into bond (in-bond) certain of its imports for the period under review. Furthermore, pursuant to a physical examination of the petitioner's factory 1,10,041 kg of raw material was found to be short in comparison to the quantity recorded in the relevant bond register. Additionally, MIS information and that collected from the lien bank reveals that though the petitioner declared its exports in 1109 EXPs, the lien bank, however, provided PRCs against only 1066 EXPs and, as such, there is no information of the remaining 43 EXPs. That shortfall, the Commissioner states, is, resultantly, of 1,54,011 kg and the material so unaccounted for is stated to have an invoice value of US$ 19,25,416. The presumption consequentially is of the said goods being illegally removed at the petitioner's behest. Moreover, the Commissioner continues, upon scrutiny of the collected EXPs in the MIS relative to the export documents of the lien bank, a discrepancy of 281 EXPs was found in respect of the extent of chemicals and fabrics utilized in the exported goods. Further, in the export information provided by the lien bank in respect of 237 EXPs, 2,88,696.51 kg products having an invoice value of US$ 30,31,146 are said to be shown short. Therefore, the total quantity of short found products is (1,54,011 + 2,88,696.51) = 4,42,707.53 kg and for the production of said short found products 31,52,741.53 kg chemicals and 5,09,113 kg fabrics were used, these having an assessable value of Taka 53,88,11,958. These are now presumed to have been illegally removed too and the amount of duty and taxes leviable on these are now assessed at Taka 29,9663,388. 

 8. Moreover, during physical inspection of the petitioner's factory premises and bonded warehouse by the investigating team, 1,10,041 kg raw material was found short in comparison to the quantity recorded in the bond register also raising the presumption that these were removed illegally. The assessable value of such short found material is Taka 2,57,65,583 attracting leviable duty and taxes totalling Taka1,24,35,244. Additionally, the Commissioner contends that 51,590 kg raw material imported against five bills of entry valued at Taka 33,88,893 is alleged not to have been in-bonded and entered in the bond register. Therefore, the total value of raw material unaccounted for stands at Taka 56,79,66,434 raising the spectre of duty and taxes evaded standing at Taka 28,33,27,833. Predicated on such discovery, the office of the Respondent No. 4, Director General, Directorate of Customs Intelligence and Investigation forwarded the investigation report to the office of the Respondent No.3 for initiating legal steps for realizing the said evaded duty/taxes and leading to the issuance of the show cause-cum-demand notice on 15-10-2019.
